title: Compose the longitudinal velocity from k to K
spoken: The longitudinal velocity in K is the moving-frame longitudinal velocity plus v, divided by one plus v times that moving-frame velocity over c squared.
explanation: This is the direction used in §5: the point's motion is given in k, and its motion in K is found. With no transverse component it becomes the collinear addition rule.
assumptions: The inertial frame k moves with signed velocity v along K's x axis, with c > 0 and |v| < c. The coordinate origins coincide at t = tau = 0 and the axes have the same normalization and orientation.
The point moves uniformly in k with components w_x and w_y, with w_x squared + w_y squared at most c squared. The inverse Lorentz time map gives t = gamma tau (1 + v w_x/c squared).
Use a nonzero elapsed time from the common origin when defining a velocity as coordinate displacement divided by elapsed time. Gamma and 1 + v w_x/c squared are positive in the admitted domain.

Modern teaching notation; the derivation projects w_x and w_y to the paper's w_xi and w_eta, gamma to beta, and c to V. The existing minus-sign velocity records describe the opposite direction K to k.

notes.title: Velocity along x in K
notes.explanation: The resulting component measured with K's rulers and clocks.

notes.title: Velocity along ξ in k
notes.explanation: The given longitudinal component measured in the moving frame k.

notes.title: Speed of k relative to K
notes.explanation: The signed frame velocity along the common longitudinal axis.

notes.title: Speed of light
notes.explanation: The positive light speed, written V in the paper and c in this teaching equation.

notes.title: The square of light speed
notes.explanation: The velocity product is divided by c squared to make a dimensionless correction.

notes.title: Frame speed times the longitudinal component
notes.explanation: Only the component parallel to the frame motion enters the time correction.

notes.title: The change in time assignment
notes.explanation: This ratio comes from the position term in the Lorentz time transformation.

notes.title: One plus the time correction
notes.explanation: Positive when the frame is subluminal and the moving point's speed does not exceed light speed.

notes.title: Given longitudinal component in k
notes.explanation: This is the same moving-frame component that enters the denominator.

notes.title: Frame speed
notes.explanation: The longitudinal frame speed adds to the given component before the time correction is applied.

notes.title: The Galilean numerator
notes.explanation: Adding the two signed longitudinal velocities supplies the numerator, but time also changes between frames.

notes.title: The component measured in K
notes.explanation: Divide the transformed displacement by the time measured in the same frame K.

notes.title: Composition from k to K
notes.explanation: The moving-frame velocity is given; the stationary-frame component is the result.

sentence.text: follows by transforming both displacement and elapsed time from k to K.
